name: Loke & Son Thermal Underlayer
description:
A long-sleeve thermal base layer that has been a staple of Great Lakes working-class wardrobes for decades. The waffle-knit fabric traps air efficiently and the flat-lock seams mean it can be worn under anything without bunching. Loke & Son makes this in twelve colors but the most common are cream, navy, and a faded red that everyone calls 'brick.' The neckline is a simple scoop — not styled, just functional. The cuffs are long enough to tuck under work gloves.

This is the shirt your grandfather wore under his overalls. It's the shirt you wear under everything from October to April. Loke & Son has made this essentially unchanged for forty years, which is either a mark of perfection or a lack of imagination depending on who you ask. Either way, it works.
what_it_says: You grew up somewhere cold. You know what actually matters in a shirt versus what's just marketing.
worn_by: anyone who works outside in the Great Lakes corridor
story_hooks: Loke & Son is one of the few remaining independent clothing manufacturers in the corridor — a corponation has made a buyout offer that the third-generation owner is struggling to refuse.
During a Shelf winter crisis, a Tier 3 aid organization is distributing these by the crate — someone is skimming the stock before it reaches distribution.
A character's only memento of a deceased mentor is a brick-red Loke & Son thermal, still folded the way the mentor always folded clothes.
